questions.prompt: Find the five-number summary of 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6, 9. Use the median of each half (lower five and upper five values) as Q1 and Q3.
questions.prompt_markup: Find the five-number summary of 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6, 9. Use the median of each half (lower five and upper five values) as Q1 and Q3.
questions.grading_note: Form required: all five values. The median is the mean of the 5th and 6th values; Q1 and Q3 are the medians of the lower and upper five values.

questions.domain: Statistics & Probability: Interpreting Categorical & Quantitative Data
questions.skill: Represent data with dot plots, histograms, and box plots
questions.standard_level: Algebra I. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Algebra I, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: For the data 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6, 9 (Q1 and Q3 are the medians of the lower five and upper five values), use the 1.5 × IQR rule to decide whether 9 is an outlier.
questions.prompt_markup: For the data 2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 5, 6, 9 (Q1 and Q3 are the medians of the lower five and upper five values), use the 1.5 × IQR rule to decide whether 9 is an outlier.
questions.correct_answer: Yes. IQR = 5 - 3 = 2, and Q3 + 1.5(2) = 8. Since 9 > 8, it is an outlier.
questions.grading_note: Form required: the answer with the fence.
